title: Karnataka High Court: A Final K-RERA Order Cannot Be Reopened by Challenging the Attachment That Follows It
case_name: M/s Unishire Promoters Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. v. State of Karnataka & Ors.
card_summary: The Karnataka High Court dismissed a writ petition by Unishire Promoters challenging the attachment of its Bengaluru property, ordered to recover dues owed to a homebuyer under a K-RERA order. The developer's appeal against that underlying order had already been dismissed, making it final. The Court held a challenge to the consequential attachment cannot be used to reopen a RERA order that has attained finality.
card_tip: Challenge a RERA recovery order within the appeal window. Once it becomes final, attacking the attachment that follows is not a back door to reopen it.
verification_notes: Decision date (6 October 2026), case number WP 6366/2025, bench (Justice E.S. Indiresh) and the holding (attachment challenge cannot reopen a final K-RERA order) corroborated across LiveLaw Biz, PropNewz and SupremeToday. The appeal's earlier dismissal date (23 August 2025) appears only in secondary reporting and is omitted from the summary.
